query: For eutectic high-entropy alloys intended for structural applications, what single intervention could simultaneously increase strength and ductility? Formulate one testable hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Hot forging at 800–900 °C followed by a short anneal at 600–700 °C will refine the lamellar eutectic microstructure of AlCoCrFeNi-type high-entropy alloys, increasing both tensile strength and ductility relative to the as-cast condition.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy (e.g., AlCoCrFeNi-based) with coarser lamellae
generation.intervention: Apply hot forging at 800–900 °C, then perform a brief anneal at 600–700 °C
generation.conditions: Process under inert atmosphere or vacuum at typical forging strain rates; recommended forging reduction of ~50% total strain followed by ~1 hour subcritical annealing
generation.structural_mediator: Refined lamellar spacing and partially recrystallized microstructure
generation.mechanism: Thermomechanical deformation and controlled recovery reduce lamellar spacing and distribute potential brittle phases, enhancing dislocation slip and retarding crack initiation to improve both strength and ductility
generation.predicted_outcome: Yield strength and elongation each increase by ~10–25% compared to the as-cast baseline at room temperature
generation.baseline: Unforged as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with coarser lamellae
generation.boundary: Applicable mainly to eutectic HEAs containing ductile/fcc and hard/bcc (or B2) phases; magnitude of improvement depends on alloy composition and forging strain rate
generation.uncertainty: Exact gains may vary with alloy purity, grain orientation, forging conditions, and minor element additions

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of as-cast eutectic HEA samples with identical composition. Subject one set to the specified forging and annealing procedure, while leaving the other in the as-cast state. Compare mechanical properties via uniaxial tensile tests.
measurements: Lamellar spacing via SEM or TEM
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermomechanically processed samples do not exhibit any measurable increase in both strength and ductility, or if lamellar refinement is not observed, the hypothesis is invalid.

cited_evidence.text: As such, our alloy design strategy resulted in the discovery of an EHEA with a fine lamellar fcc/B2 structure and balanced high fracture strength and high ductility. This novel strategy is promising to solve the problems inhibiting the engineering application of HEAs as high-temperature materials, including the inferior castability and compositional segregation, and the conflict between high fracture strength and high ductility. In addition, this novel strategy also brought breakthrough to NiAl-based alloys in significantly enhancing the ductility at room temperature while simultaneously achieving the high strength. The EHEA concept, combining the advantages of both HEAs and eutectic alloys, and at the same time eliminating the disadvantages of these two types of alloys, leads to a promising new class of high-temperature alloys. Using this new alloy design strategy, an industrial scale HEA with uniform organizations and compositions can be prepared by the conventional casting method in a low cost way, allowing for large-scale industrial applications.
